subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should ordinary Discord routed replies support visible identity overrides, and if so should the approved model be webhook persona delivery, bot self-profile mutation, binding nickname config, or deferral?
rationale: The request changes a stable public config surface and a credential-backed Discord identity boundary, so automation should not choose the product/security model.

options.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
options.body: Implement a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path using explicit webhook credentials, username/avatar validation, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Coordinate with self-profile work
options.body: Treat this as dependent on the broader Discord self-profile decision at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 before adding a separate binding field.

options.title: Defer binding identity overrides
options.body: Keep the core behavior unchanged and document multi-account or thread-bound alternatives until maintainers want a new identity surface.

recommendation.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
recommendation.body: Implement a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path using explicit webhook credentials, username/avatar validation, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent thread-bound Discord routing and webhook identity path most likely to shape this decision.
